daytona-shim: Daytona Championship USA without TeknoParrot
===========================================================

Runs the original game, the 2019 New Season Edition and the 2017 edition,
on Windows and on the Steam Deck, with modern pads, wheels and force
feedback, and a full-screen launcher for the game's settings.

Status: test build. Both editions run on the Steam Deck. Not yet tried on
real hardware: wheels and force feedback.


Quick start
-----------
1. Make a folder for the game and unzip everything from this zip into it.
2. Unpack each edition into a subfolder of it (see 1 below).
3. Windows: double-click DaytonaLauncher.exe.
   Steam Deck: add DaytonaLauncher.exe to Steam as a non-Steam game, force
   Proton Experimental (or 9 or later) under Compatibility, and set its
   Launch Options to:
       WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b" %command%
   (Without it Proton uses its own dinput8 and the shim is not loaded.)


1. Set up the folders
---------------------
One folder for the game holds everything from this zip; each edition is
unpacked into a subfolder of it. The same layout works on Windows and the
Deck:

    Daytona/                         e.g. C:\Games\Daytona on Windows,
      DaytonaLauncher.exe                 /home/deck/Games/Daytona on the Deck
      dinput8.dll
      SDL3.dll
      shim.ini
      INSTALL.txt, licences
      2019/                          the 2019 download's contents
        Sega/Daytona/Daytona.exe
      2017/                          the 2017 download's contents
        Daytona/Daytona.exe
                Daytona.exe.original (keep it: see below)

The launcher finds the editions by itself (it looks four folders down from
its own). When you START an edition, it copies dinput8.dll, SDL3.dll and
shim.ini next to that edition's Daytona.exe: the two DLLs whenever its own
are newer (to update, replace them in the top folder), shim.ini only the
first time (it holds that edition's controls). With only one edition,
leave out the other subfolder.

The 2017 folder's Daytona.exe is TeknoParrot's patched copy; the original
is beside it as Daytona.exe.original. Keep both: the shim reads the
original and puts its code back in memory. Neither file is changed.

If the editions are somewhere else, name the folders that hold each
Daytona.exe in a launcher.ini next to the launcher, relative to it or
absolute:
    [Editions]
    2019=2019\Sega\Daytona
    2017=2017\Daytona
(Under Proton, Linux paths are on drive Z:. /home/deck/Games is
Z:\home\deck\Games.)

Close TeknoParrot first if it is running (its shell takes the same port).
To remove everything, delete the top folder's files and the dinput8.dll,
SDL3.dll and shim.ini the launcher copied next to each Daytona.exe. The
shim changes nothing else in the game folders; the launcher changes the
game's own settings files only when you save, and keeps the first version
of each beside it as .shim-backup.


2. Windows
----------
Double-click DaytonaLauncher.exe. It opens full screen (see 4) and works
with a pad or the keyboard. You can make a shortcut to it, or add it to
Steam as a non-Steam game (no launch options needed on Windows).

Once the launcher has started an edition, its Daytona.exe can also be
started directly; the shim beside it loads either way.


3. Steam Deck (Desktop Mode)
----------------------------
1. Steam > Games > Add a Non-Steam Game to My Library > Browse, pick
   DaytonaLauncher.exe in the top folder (set the file type filter to
   "All Files" if it is hidden).
2. In the new entry's Properties:
   - Compatibility: tick "Force the use of a specific Steam Play
     compatibility tool", choose Proton Experimental (or 9 or later).
   - Launch Options (needed: without it Proton uses its own dinput8 and
     the shim is not loaded):
         WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b" %command%
     To skip the launcher and start the last edition chosen at once:
         WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b" %command% --play
3. Launch it (Game Mode works too).

If Steam calls the game "Spacewar" and uses that game's controller layout,
a steam_appid.txt (app 480, from another package) is in a game folder.
Delete it (and steam_api.dll or a steam_settings folder if present).


4. The launcher
---------------
It opens full screen at the screen's own resolution (1280x800 on the
Deck, 1920x1080 or anything else on a PC):

  Title     the logo, the edition (left / right to switch, when both are
            installed), START, OPTIONS and CONTROLS
  OPTIONS   one list: free play, volumes and every rule of the game
  CONTROLS  the pad's actions, the wheel's axes, buttons, steering scale
            and pedals, and force feedback / rumble (the edition's
            shim.ini). A (Cross) on a pad action or a wheel axis or button
            waits for you to press the button, or move the stick, trigger,
            wheel or pedal, you want; Esc on a keyboard cancels. The top of
            the screen shows what the game will get from your wheel.

  Move: d-pad or left stick (arrows on a keyboard); change a setting:
  left / right; select: A (Cross on PlayStation, Enter); back: B (Circle,
  Esc or Backspace). B on the title screen closes the launcher. Settings
  are saved when you leave a list. The button prompts follow the pad you
  use.

Its sounds and music are the game's own, read from the game folder: the
name panel sound when moving, "decision" and "cancel", the engine revving
as the game starts, and the select music in a seamless loop at 80% of the
game's music volume.

Options:
  --play     start the last edition chosen at once
  --desktop  a plain window with tabs instead (Game, Rules, Controller,
             Wheel, and the edition at the top right)


5. Controls in the game
-----------------------
Pads: Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and others (through SDL3.dll), and the
Deck's own controls through Steam Input. The default layout, by button
position:
  Steering        left stick
  Gas / brake     right / left trigger
  Start           Start / Options / +
  Coin            Back / Share / -
  Shift up/down   right / left bumper
  Views 1-4       top / left / right / bottom button (Xbox: Y / X / B / A)
  Quit            hold Start + Back for a second
Several controllers at once are combined. Change the layout in the
launcher's CONTROLS, or in shim.ini [Pad].

Keyboard: arrows (steer, gas, brake), Enter start, 5 coin, A / Z shift,
F1-F4 views, Esc quits.

Wheels: Logitech, Thrustmaster, Fanatec and other wheels SDL knows are
used by themselves. The defaults suit a Logitech G29 / G923: paddles shift,
Options is Start, Share is Coin, the H-shifter's gears 1-4. For another
wheel, map it in CONTROLS. If full lock needs too much rotation, set about
270 degrees in the wheel's software or raise the steering scale.

Force feedback: the game's own force feedback (what drove the cabinet's
motor) goes to a wheel as a constant force and to pads as rumble. Set the
strength, turn it off or reverse it in CONTROLS.

Free play is on by default; turn it off in OPTIONS to play with coins.


6. If something goes wrong
--------------------------
The shim writes shim.log next to each Daytona.exe. Please send it along
with what happened. A good run shows, in this order:
  hook WS2_32.dll!#4 ... (and the other hooks)
  shell: listening on 127.0.0.1:18888
  shell: game connected
  shell: <- 0x.. / shell: -> 0x2C (the greeting)
  pad: SDL 3.x.x, then "pad: <name> connected as a pad / wheel"
  CreateProcessA(c:\sega\shell\InpWrapper.exe ...): the shim is the force-feedback helper
  ffb: registered with the game window: yes
  (2017) restore: ... ranges (... bytes) put back from Daytona.exe.original, 0 skipped
  dinput: CreateDevice(SEGA IO Controller)
  shell: <- 0x2A (... challenge) every 10 s, each answered with -> 0x2E

If SDL causes trouble (a pad missing or doubled), SDL=0 in shim.ini goes
back to XInput pads only.
